Metadata.title: avalis – The Digital Solution for Accommodation Processes at Swiss Universities
Metadata.description: avalis is a digital solution for the accommodation process at Swiss universities.

Footer.tagline: A digital solution for the accommodation process at Swiss universities.

Hero.lead: avalis is a digital solution for the accommodation process at Swiss universities. It bundles the path from request to implementation, simplified, transparent and modularly adaptable.

Team.headline: Three perspectives. One shared concern.
Team.lead: Behind avalis are Chiara Tremml, Dario Foti and Mike De Bastiani, a three-person team with a UX design background. The video shows what motivated the team to take on this project and what avalis solves.

Solution.headline: One shared place for a complex process.
Solution.intro: An accommodation measure allows students with disabilities adapted study and exam conditions. The path there runs through several instances, from the request through advice and approval to implementation, and is fragmented, resource-intensive and marked by breaks between media today. Based on nationwide research and a consistently user-centred design process, avalis bundles this process and connects all the instances involved.

students.title: Clearly guided, requests visible at all times
students.body: Students submit their request digitally once and can track its status at any time. The process guides them step by step from submission to the final decision. Sensitive details stay protected and are only shared with the parties involved.

advisory.title: A digital case management system in one place
advisory.body: Advisory offices manage every case in one structured system: reviewing requests, coordinating advisory appointments, recording feedback. Manual back-and-forth by email disappears. Communication between everyone involved stays traceable and documented in avalis.

decision.title: Structured, with decisions generated automatically
decision.body: Decision-making bodies receive reviewed requests with all relevant documents and enter their decision directly in the system. The formal decision is generated automatically based on it.

Modularity.title: Adaptable and flexible for every university
Modularity.body: Swiss universities organise the accommodation process differently. Designed as a modular web prototype, avalis can be adapted flexibly to each university's existing process structures and institutional responsibilities.

Prototype.title: From request to decision.
Prototype.context: The web prototype walkthrough gives an overview of the solution and how the instances involved work together.
Prototype.disclaimerBody: The walkthrough shows the process using a fictional example at the University of Zurich (UZH). It is not a productive system of the UZH. All data shown is fictional.
Prototype.statusNote: Development status: a functional web prototype tested with subject-matter experts. Not intended for productive use.

Registration.title: Understand the accommodation process better.
Registration.lead1: A nationwide survey across 17 universities through interviews, questionnaires and an analysis of official process documents.
Registration.lead2: How does the accommodation process actually work? Where are its limits? And what does that mean for a digital solution?

privacy.intro: Protecting your personal data matters to us. This policy explains which data we process when you visit the avalis website, register for the Research Report or contact us.

blocks.p: The controller for the processing of personal data on this website is the avalis project team (“we”). You can reach us at <mail>{email}</mail>.
We comply with the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP). Where the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies, we also observe its requirements.

When you open the website, our hosting provider processes technically necessary connection data: IP address, date and time, the page requested, the amount of data transferred, and information about your browser and operating system. This data is needed to run and secure the website. We do not analyse it on a personal basis.
We currently do not use any analytics or tracking tools.

blocks.h: When you register for the Research Report

blocks.p: When you submit the registration form, we process the following information:

ul: Email address (required)
Educational institution (required, free text)
Role (required; if you choose “Other”, the description you enter)
First name and last name (optional)
Origin of your visit (“network meeting”, “mail” or “direct”), if you reached the page through a corresponding link or QR code
Time of registration (recorded automatically by Brevo)

blocks.p: Please do not enter any sensitive personal data (for example health data) in the free-text fields.

blocks.h: When we send the report email

blocks.p: We send you the link to the Research Report exclusively by email to the address you provided. The link is not shown on the website. When sending, Brevo records technical delivery information (for example whether the email could be delivered). We do not track whether or when you open the email or click on links.

The unsubscribe link in the report email contains your email address (encoded) and a digital signature. Its sole purpose is to remove you from the mailing list securely. You are only unsubscribed once you click “Unsubscribe now” on the unsubscribe page. Search engines do not index this page.

blocks.h: When you contact us by email

blocks.p: If you write to us, we process your sender address, your message and the information it contains in order to respond to your request. Our mailbox is operated by Google (Gmail).

ul: Operating and securing the website: we have a legitimate interest in a functioning and secure website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Delivering the Research Report and occasional updates about avalis: the basis is your consent, given by ticking the box in the form (Art. 31(1) FADP; Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR).

Evaluating which institutions, roles and channels show interest in avalis: we only evaluate this information in aggregated form and do not publish individual details (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Answering enquiries by email: legitimate interest in appropriate communication (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Playing videos: your consent, given by clicking “Play” (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR).

blocks.p: We do not use your data for third-party advertising and do not make automated individual decisions. No profiling takes place.

We do not sell your data and do not pass it on to third parties for their own purposes. We use the following service providers, who process data on our behalf and are contractually bound to data protection:

ul: <brevo>Brevo</brevo> (provider based in the EU): storing registration data in our contact list and sending the report email. According to Brevo, the data is stored in the EU.
<vercel>Vercel Inc.</vercel> (USA): hosting the website, delivering pages and receiving the registration form.

<google>Google</google>: the Research Report is provided via Google Drive. When you open the link in the email, you visit a Google page. Google then processes data such as your IP address under its own responsibility. Google also operates our mailbox (Gmail).
YouTube (a Google service): see “Embedded videos”.

blocks.p: Only members of the avalis project team have access to the data. Beyond that, we only disclose data if we are legally obliged to or an authority requires it.

Vercel and Google are based in the USA, so data may be transferred there. Both companies are certified under the Swiss-U.S. and EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. For certified companies, the USA is considered to provide an adequate level of data protection. Where data is transferred beyond that to countries without an adequate level of protection, this takes place on the basis of suitable safeguards, in particular recognised standard contractual clauses.
Brevo is based in the EU, which Switzerland recognises as providing an adequate level of data protection. Brevo may in turn use sub-processors; details are in Brevo’s data protection documentation.

ul: Our hosting provider stores connection data (server logs) only as long as needed for operation and security.

We store registration data until you unsubscribe or request deletion, at the latest until the avalis project ends. After that we delete it, unless you have expressly agreed that we may continue to use it.
We keep emails sent to us for as long as needed to handle your request or as required by law.

blocks.p: When you unsubscribe, we remove you from the mailing list and you receive no further emails. If you also want us to delete the rest of your information completely, send us a short note at <mail>{email}</mail>.

We do not use tracking or advertising cookies. The website only stores your language choice in a technically necessary cookie (NEXT_LOCALE). It contains only the selected language and is deleted when you close the browser. No consent is required for this.
The DM Sans font is hosted locally and delivered from our own server. There is no connection to Google Fonts.

Two YouTube videos are embedded on the website. At first you only see a preview image, which is loaded through our own server. Simply visiting the page therefore does not make your browser connect to YouTube.

Only when you click “Play” do we load the video in enhanced privacy mode (youtube-nocookie.com). Google, which operates YouTube, then receives your IP address and information about your browser and may store cookies or similar technologies on your device. By clicking, you consent to this processing. How Google processes data is described in the <google>Google Privacy Policy</google>. If you do not want this, do not click “Play”.

We take appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect your data. These include encrypted transmission (HTTPS), server-side processing of the form, spam protection and signed unsubscribe links. Email communication is not encrypted end to end. Complete security cannot be guaranteed on the internet.
Under the FADP and, where applicable, the GDPR, you have the following rights:

ul: Access to whether and which personal data we process about you
Rectification of inaccurate data
Erasure or restriction of processing
Objection to processing based on our legitimate interest
Receiving your data in a common electronic format
Withdrawal of your consent at any time with effect for the future: via the unsubscribe link in the report email or by email. Processing carried out before remains lawful.

blocks.p: To exercise your rights, write to us at <mail>{email}</mail>. We may ask for proof of identity and will usually reply within 30 days.
Providing your email address, institution and role is necessary so that we can deliver the report to you. Without them, registration is not possible. All other information is optional.

You may lodge a complaint with a data protection authority. In Switzerland this is the <edoeb>Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC)</edoeb>. Visitors from the EU may contact the supervisory authority of their country of residence.
We may update this privacy policy, for example when we extend the website or use new services. The version published here applies.
